about.title: Del Mar Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Del Mar is a small coastal city, but its roads still see their share of collisions. Public records show 17 injury crashes and 22 injured people in the most recent full year, with Friday midday hours around 12 to 2 p.m. showing up often in the data. Camino Del Mar, Via De La Valle, Del Mar Heights Road, and Carmel Valley Road are the corridors that appear most in these reports, likely a reflection of local traffic patterns rather than anything about the roads themselves. If you were hurt in a crash on one of these streets or anywhere else in town, the days right after matter. Insurance adjusters move fast, and details fade. Our team helps you get started quickly, gathering evidence and speaking with insurers on your behalf, while you focus on getting better.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Again

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity was involved, such as a city vehicle. We can flag deadlines early so nothing is missed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage you're found responsible, even partly. An insurer may try to shift blame onto you during a recorded statement, so it helps to have someone guiding what you say.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Actually Lost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a typical car accident case. We work on contingency, meaning no fee unless you recover, and can push for the full value of your claim without upfront cost to you.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can help you understand what, if anything, you should say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on Camino Del Mar or another busy corridor?
items.answer: Whether it happened on Camino Del Mar, Via De La Valle, or a quieter side street, the same evidence-preservation steps apply: photos, witness contacts, and prompt medical care. Local corridors with more reported crashes simply mean more documented incidents, not that any single crash is treated differently under the law. We can help gather traffic camera footage or reports that may exist for these higher-traffic areas.

items.question: How much does it cost to work with an attorney?
items.answer: We offer a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover compensation for you. You don't pay anything upfront to have your case reviewed.
